defects.title: _require_board_rule is a board-composition check, not a format check: it rejects any legitimately main-board-only symbol subset, so LimitWidth/BoardCode die on --max-symbols and on an explicit symbols=[...] view
defects.failure_scenario: The guard fires when no STAR/GEM/BSE prefix is present, but a correctly spelled, all-main-board symbol list is a normal input, not a format error. Reproduced (/Users/wxy/Desktop/Partura/tmp/impl/review_WP2/a7_subset_repro.py): with WP3's own planned synthetic spelling ([f"{600000+i}.SH" for i in range(12)] + 688001.SH / 300001.SZ / 830001.BJ) the FULL list derives fine (15,12), but store.view(max_symbols=4|8|12) -> sym_idx[:k] (store.py:215) yields a main-board-only prefix and df.resolve('LimitWidth', sub, dates) raises ValueError; so does a hand-picked real list ['600000.SH','600036.SH','601398.SH','000001.SZ'] for BOTH LimitWidth and BoardCode. max_symbols is a live CLI argument reaching warmed_view (research.py:84 -> store.view(..., max_symbols=...)) from cli.py:81/99/140, scripts/check_store.py:30, scripts/diagnose_run.py:52, scripts/compare_daily_store.py:126, scripts/eval_legacy_factors.py:136; tests/test_store.py:22 already does store.view(max_symbols=4). Once WP3's CubeView.daily(name) calls resolve() with self.symbols/self.dates, every factor touching LimitWidth or BoardCode raises on such a view instead of evaluating. Extending the guard to BoardCode (the stated deviation) doubles the blast radius.
defects.suggested_fix: Split the two questions. Keep a cheap FORMAT check per call: raise only when the symbol list cannot be prefix-first at all, e.g. `if not any(str(s)[:1].isdigit() for s in symbols): raise ValueError(...)` — verified to return False for ['SH.600000', ...] and True for the bank subset, so it catches must_fix #2's real failure without depending on board composition. Move the 'at least one STAR/GEM/BSE rule actually fired' assertion to where the full universe is in hand: WP3's CubeStore/SegmentedCubeStore daily-source attach (over store.symbols) and WP9's build script, which already prints the symbol lists and enforces a coverage floor. If per-call strictness is wanted, downgrade the composition case to a warnings.warn so a subset view degrades loudly instead of crashing.

defects.title: The late-start guard provably cannot fire in the one case it was written for: a 100% label mismatch between the daily store and the view returns an all-NaN plane with no warning
defects.failure_scenario: _warn_once_if_late_start returns early when finite_days.size == 0, i.e. exactly when the plane is entirely NaN. Reproduced (/Users/wxy/Desktop/Partura/tmp/impl/review_WP2/a2_silent_allnan.py): a DailyFieldStore whose meta.json spells symbols 'SH.600000'-style while the view asks '600000.SH'-style gives df.resolve('FloatCap', view_syms, dates, store=store) -> 'finite cells: 0 of 9, warnings raised: []'. The same for a date-format mismatch ('2020-01-01' vs '20200101'): 0 finite, 0 warnings. This is the identical silent failure the design's must_fix #2 part 3 describes for tearsheet.load_caps ('a format mismatch NaNs every cell silently') and the 'silently-empty-warm-up' entry in Risks — the stored-field half of the same bug. Worse, one single finite cell is enough to silence it completely: a plane whose only finite value is at [0,0] (99% NaN) produced 'finite 1, warnings: 0', so a daily store covering 3 of 5000 symbols warns about nothing and every factor built on it quietly evaluates on a near-empty panel.
defects.suggested_fix: In _warn_once_if_late_start, replace the `if finite_days.size == 0: return` early exit with a warning of its own ('daily field %r has no finite value anywhere in the requested range [%s, %s]: the store's symbol/date spelling probably does not match the view's'), and add a coverage test next to the first-finite-date test, e.g. `cov = float(np.isfinite(plane).mean())` warning below a low floor (say 0.01). Both are one-liners inside a function WP2 already owns; the guard's existing message and stacklevel can be reused.

defects.title: test_derive_list_age_prefers_status_over_tradable does not test its own claim: the status-over-tradable priority stays green when inverted
defects.failure_scenario: The test's docstring states 'status is the richer signal and must win when both are given', but it never passes both — it calls derive(status=...) and derive(tradable=...) separately on inputs where the two AGREE and asserts the results are equal, which holds under either priority. Verified by mutation (/Users/wxy/Desktop/Partura/tmp/impl/review_WP2/mutplugin.py, MUT=1 swaps _lifecycle_mask to check tradable first): `MUT=1 pytest tests/test_daily_leaf_typing.py -q` -> 66 passed. The unpinned behaviour is not cosmetic: with both given and disagreeing (status=[[OUTSIDE,TRADING,TRADING]], tradable=[[True,True,True]]) the real code returns [nan, 0, 1] and the inverted code returns [10000, 10001, 10002] — a listing date off by one day and a 10000 sentinel where there should be none. WP3's CubeView.daily() is precisely the caller that has both view.tradable() and view.day_status() in hand, so a WP3 implementer who passes both and then refactors _lifecycle_mask has no test standing in the way.
defects.suggested_fix: Rewrite the test to pass BOTH kwargs with a disagreeing pair and assert the status answer: `status = np.array([[O, T, T]], dtype=np.int8); tradable = np.array([[True, True, True]]); np.testing.assert_array_equal(df.derive('ListAge', ['A'], dates, status=status, tradable=tradable)[0], [np.nan, 0.0, 1.0])` (use assert_array_equal with nan-aware comparison or check isnan separately). Keep the existing agreeing-inputs assertion as a second case if desired.

defects.title: test_resolve_log_field_logs_the_float64_plane_before_casting cannot discriminate log-before-cast from log-after-cast, so the one structural contract the design names for the log fields is unpinned
defects.failure_scenario: The test compares got against np.log(plane).astype(np.float32), which is byte-identical to the mutation it is supposed to exclude. Verified two ways: (a) direct arithmetic on the fixture's own numbers — max abs diff between np.log(f64).astype(f32) and np.log(f64.astype(f32)).astype(f32) is exactly 0.0, and still 0.0 at a realistic 1e12 cap with a 1e-3 move (/Users/wxy/Desktop/Partura/tmp/impl/review_WP2/a4_more_mutations.py); (b) mutation MUT=3 replaces resolve()'s log branch with cast-then-log and `pytest tests/test_daily_leaf_typing.py -q` -> 66 passed. So if a later package 'simplifies' resolve() to cast first, nothing goes red, and WP2's own docstring then describes a step the code no longer takes.
defects.suggested_fix: Either pin the step structurally rather than numerically — assert on store.plane(base).dtype == np.float64 and that resolve's intermediate is float64 (e.g. monkeypatch np.log with a recorder and assert the array it received was float64) — or build the fixture plane at a magnitude where the two differ (a value near float32's subnormal/overflow range, or 1+2**-30 where float32 rounds to 1.0 and log goes to exactly 0.0) and keep the numeric comparison. Alternatively, given the implementer's own measurement that the step is immaterial, drop the claim from the test name and say in one line that the step is kept for the design's structural contract, not for precision.

defects.title: Design step 6 (resolve warns on a late-starting field) has no end-to-end test: removing resolve()'s guard call leaves the WP2 file fully green, and the one test named for it asserts the opposite
defects.failure_scenario: test_warn_once_message_fires_only_when_the_field_starts_late calls df._warn_once_if_late_start directly, never through resolve(); test_resolve_warns_when_a_stored_field_starts_after_the_requested_range, despite its name, asserts that NO warning fires (simplefilter('error') over a fixture that is deliberately not a late start). Verified by mutation: /Users/wxy/Desktop/Partura/tmp/impl/review_WP2/mut8.py reimplements resolve() identically minus the _warn_once_if_late_start call; `PYTHONPATH=... pytest tests/test_daily_leaf_typing.py -q -p mut8` -> 66 passed. So the wiring between the guard and the resolver — the whole of design step 6 — is unprotected, and WP3/WP9 can lose it in a refactor without a red test.
defects.suggested_fix: Add a stored field to the daily_store fixture whose first finite COLUMN is late (e.g. a second plane with arr[:, :2] = np.nan) and assert through the public API: `with pytest.warns(RuntimeWarning, match='no finite value before'): df.resolve('TotalCap', symbols, dates, store=store)`. Also rename test_resolve_warns_when_a_stored_field_starts_after_the_requested_range to say what it actually asserts (that a single missing CELL is not a late start).

defects.title: fingerprint()'s docstring overclaims: bumping DERIVED_VERSION invalidates nothing when no daily store is attached, which is exactly the configuration in which the three derived fields are still fully resolvable
defects.failure_scenario: fingerprint(None) returns None (correct, and required for byte-identical contract_hash / ExemplarCache keys), but resolve('LimitWidth'|'BoardCode'|'ListAge', ..., store=None) works with no store at all — tested by test_resolve_derived_field_needs_no_store. So a run that mines with LimitWidth on a store with no daily_root gets fingerprint None, and the docstring's promise that 'a later change to derive()'s formulas (bump DERIVED_VERSION) invalidates cached rank fingerprints without the caller doing anything' is false in precisely that case: mining/rankban.py:242-249 view_cache_key hashes only dates[0], dates[-1], len(dates), n_symbols and the two sample sizes, so after a derive() change the on-disk ExemplarCache silently serves rank fingerprints computed under the old LimitWidth/ListAge definition.
defects.suggested_fix: Minimum, inside WP2: correct the docstring to say the DERIVED_VERSION mix-in only takes effect when a daily store is attached, and that a derive() change must be accompanied by deleting the exemplar cache when it is not. Better, and the right note to hand WP3/WP7: have the view pass `f"{DERIVED_VERSION}"` (not None) once any daily field is actually read, i.e. key on 'were daily fields used' rather than 'is a store attached' — that keeps every existing key byte-identical (no daily field read => still None) while closing the hole.

defects.title: fingerprint() hashes only meta.json, so rewriting a daily plane leaves contract_hash and the ExemplarCache view key byte-identical
defects.failure_scenario: meta_sha256 = _sha256_file(root/'meta.json') covers labels and the field list only, never daily_<name>.npy. Reproduced (/Users/wxy/Desktop/Partura/tmp/impl/review_WP2/a4_more_mutations.py): np.save over daily_FloatCap.npy with completely different values, reopen DailyFieldStore -> 'fingerprint stable across a silent data rewrite: True' while plane() returns the new values. Via WP3's contract_hash change and WP7's ExemplarCache key, a corrected cap rebuild that does not happen to touch meta.json is indistinguishable from the old one: calculate.py's recorded provenance hash is wrong and cached rank fingerprints from the old data are served. (The design does specify f"{DERIVED_VERSION}:{store.meta_sha256}", so the shape of the fix is a writer-side obligation, not a change to this signature.)
defects.suggested_fix: Nothing to change in fingerprint()'s signature; instead make meta.json carry the data identity so meta_sha256 moves with it. Add one line to WP2's DailyFieldStore docstring stating that meta.json MUST include each plane's own sha256 (or a build id), and make that explicit in WP9's build_daily_fields.py: write {'fields': [...], 'symbols': [...], 'dates': [...], 'planes': {name: sha256(daily_<name>.npy)}}. Optionally have DailyFieldStore verify a plane against its recorded digest on first load.

result.notes:
范围与门禁(都通过)
- 只碰了清单内 4 个文件:src/alphacube/dailyfields.py、src/alphacube/expression.py、src/alphacube/parser.py、tests/test_daily_leaf_typing.py;git status 干净。
- 全套测试:705 passed, 10 skipped, 1 xfailed(=617 基线 + WP1/WP6 的 22 + WP2 的 66),无新失败。
- 设计 WP2 的 10 个步骤逐条都实现了,签名与设计里声明的 API 一字不差(derive / DailyFieldStore.plane|align|fields|meta_sha256|symbols|dates / resolve / available / fingerprint,关键字全是 keyword-only)。parser 的六处重命名全部到位,没有残留 self.daily_fields。

默认参数下的行为与随机数流:用摘要对比了基线树(/Users/wxy/Desktop/AlphaCube,517fd09)和本树,**逐字节相同**(脚本 /Users/wxy/Desktop/Partura/tmp/impl/review_WP2/a5_compat.py):1498 条 legacy corpus 的 n_parsed=1442 / n_errors=56 / unknown_field=33、已解析表达式 key 摘要、错误键摘要、TypedTreeGenerator(seed=12345) 120 棵种群摘要、五个 mutate_* 加 crossover 的摘要、每段之后的 RNG 状态、gen.fields 仍是 8、searchable 仍是 218/214。新分支都挂在 `spec.needs_full_m` 下并以 `isinstance(operand, DailyFeature)` 为条件,而 DailyFeature 只有新加的 parser 分支能造出来,所以旧路径一次也进不去,也不多取随机数。另外确认 legacy corpus 里没有任何 circ_mv/total_mv/float_cap/board 之类标识符,所以新命名空间没有把原本解析失败的因子变成能解析(这点我专门查了,是最可能的兼容性破口)。

实现者三条 deviation 我独立核过,都成立
- cs_bucket_rank / cs_winsor 确实不在 default_registry(),它们在 partura/ops_ext.py:793 的 NEW_OPERATORS 里;替换用的 cs_regres 是 nd/cs/binary、needs_daily、非 trivial_boolean、非 non_root,替换合理。
- 精度那条**是对的,而且 WP3 会踩**:用真 nd_ts.ts_delta 在 float32 上扫 cap∈{1e9,1e12,1e13} × move∈{1e-2..1e-5},12 格全是 raw FloatCap 误差更小,倍数约等于 log(cap)(脚本 a6_precision.py)。设计 WP3 测试计划那句「ts_delta(LogFloatCap,1) 把 1e-3 的日变动还原到优于 1e-5 相对误差,而 ts_delta(FloatCap,1) 做不到」两半都假:LogFloatCap 实测 4.97e-5(不优于 1e-5),FloatCap 实测 1.38e-5(反而更好)。**请让 WP3 的实现者删掉或重写这条测试,照抄必红。**
- BoardCode 的 0/1/2/3 编码确实是设计没定的,导出四个常量的做法可以;掩码施加顺序(star→gem→bse,bse 最后)和 tradability.py:23-29 的 board_limit 一致,而且三组前缀两两不交,所以 LimitWidth/BoardCode 不会打架。
- _list_age 对照 partura/ops_ext.py:779-789 的 cross_age 逐行核过:公式一样(age+old),只是 isfinite→lifecycle 掩码、axis 0→axis 1。注意**day-0 老股的值是 10000+d 而不是常数 10000**;WP3 测试计划写的是「sentinel for a day-0 stock」,实现者若直接断言 == LIST_AGE_SENTINEL 只有第 0 天成立,请提醒。

另外两件不够格单列、但 WP3 应该知道的
- _lifecycle_mask 的形状检查只比 (S, D);当 S == D(方阵视图)时传反的 (D, S) 面会静默通过。WP3 传 view.day_status()/view.tradable() 时最好另加一次 orientation 断言。
- dailyfields.py 把 OUTSIDE_LIFECYCLE 硬编码成 0,而 store.py:106 的 `self._codes = {**DAY_STATUS_CODES, **self.meta.get("day_status_codes", {})}` 是可被 meta 覆盖的,CubeView.tradable()(store.py:439)就尊重这个覆盖。仓库内目前只写默认值,所以不算缺陷;但 WP3 的 daily() 要么传已经布尔化的 in-lifecycle 掩码,要么把 code 值也传进来,别让两边的约定分叉。

测试质量小结(第 4 项)
66 条新测试里,我用变异逐条验过的真测试有:shape 单例恒等(MUT=4 红)、operand_ok 的双模式拒绝(MUT=2 红)、BoardCode 的格式守卫(MUT=5 红)、align 按标签而非按位置(MUT=6 红)、受限 Registry 下的别名再校验、LimitWidth 的转置与连续性。假的/测不到的三处已写进 defects(ListAge 优先级、log-before-cast、resolve 的告警接线)。还有一点口径差异不算缺陷但记一下:设计说 day_sum(FloatCap) 等三例应在两种模式下抛 ShapeError,测试断言的是 parser 包装后的 ParseError,从未直接对 make_node 断言 ShapeError —— 而 TypedTreeGenerator 走的正是 make_node;虽然逻辑同源,补一条直接的 make_node 断言会更贴近搜索路径。
